📦 Section 1 — Setup & Synthetic Data Generation¶

Generating realistic 10-year enrollment data for a technical computer institute.

In [2]:
# ── Configuration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
np.random.seed(42)

YEARS = list(range(2015, 2025))

FIELDS = [
    'Web Development',
    'Cyber Security',
    'AI / Machine Learning',
    'Data Science',
    'Cloud Computing',
    'Mobile App Dev',
    'Graphic Design / UI-UX'
]

FIELD_COLORS = {
    'Web Development':         '#2196F3',
    'Cyber Security':          '#F44336',
    'AI / Machine Learning':   '#9C27B0',
    'Data Science':            '#FF9800',
    'Cloud Computing':         '#00BCD4',
    'Mobile App Dev':          '#4CAF50',
    'Graphic Design / UI-UX':  '#795548',
}

# ── Dataset 1: Yearly Institute Totals ────────────────────────────────────────
# Simulates organic growth from 180 (2015) → 1,020 (2024)
TOTAL_STUDENTS = [180, 215, 268, 330, 405, 472, 520, 598, 775, 1020]

yearly_data = {
    'Year': YEARS,
    'Total_Students':  TOTAL_STUDENTS,
    'New_Enrollments': [int(s * np.random.uniform(0.58, 0.68)) for s in TOTAL_STUDENTS],
    'Completions':     [int(s * np.random.uniform(0.50, 0.60)) for s in TOTAL_STUDENTS],
    'Dropouts':        [int(s * np.random.uniform(0.06, 0.10)) for s in TOTAL_STUDENTS],
}

yearly_df = pd.DataFrame(yearly_data)

# Derived KPIs
yearly_df['Retention_Rate_pct'] = (
    (1 - yearly_df['Dropouts'] / yearly_df['Total_Students']) * 100
).round(1)

yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct'] = (
    yearly_df['Total_Students'].pct_change() * 100
).round(1).fillna(0.0)

# ── Dataset 2: Field-wise Enrollment ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Each field has its own growth trajectory reflecting real industry demand shifts

FIELD_BASE = {
    'Web Development':        48,
    'Cyber Security':         18,
    'AI / Machine Learning':   8,
    'Data Science':           10,
    'Cloud Computing':        14,
    'Mobile App Dev':         28,
    'Graphic Design / UI-UX': 22,
}

# Annual growth multipliers (higher = faster growth in that year)
FIELD_GROWTH = {
    'Web Development':         [1.09, 1.11, 1.12, 1.10, 1.08, 1.07, 1.06, 1.11, 1.13, 1.11],
    'Cyber Security':          [1.14, 1.18, 1.22, 1.24, 1.26, 1.22, 1.20, 1.30, 1.38, 1.32],
    'AI / Machine Learning':   [1.18, 1.24, 1.30, 1.36, 1.42, 1.36, 1.22, 1.48, 1.65, 1.58],
    'Data Science':            [1.16, 1.20, 1.26, 1.30, 1.36, 1.28, 1.18, 1.42, 1.58, 1.52],
    'Cloud Computing':         [1.12, 1.16, 1.20, 1.24, 1.28, 1.22, 1.16, 1.32, 1.42, 1.38],
    'Mobile App Dev':          [1.10, 1.12, 1.14, 1.12, 1.10, 1.08, 1.07, 1.11, 1.13, 1.11],
    'Graphic Design / UI-UX':  [1.08, 1.10, 1.12, 1.13, 1.11, 1.10, 1.08, 1.12, 1.14, 1.12],
}

FIELD_FEES_PKR = {
    'Web Development':        15000,
    'Cyber Security':         25000,
    'AI / Machine Learning':  30000,
    'Data Science':           28000,
    'Cloud Computing':        22000,
    'Mobile App Dev':         18000,
    'Graphic Design / UI-UX': 12000,
}

field_records = []
for field in FIELDS:
    count = FIELD_BASE[field]
    for i, year in enumerate(YEARS):
        if i > 0:
            count = int(count * FIELD_GROWTH[field][i])
        field_records.append({
            'Year':                year,
            'Field':               field,
            'Students':            count,
            'Completion_Rate_pct': round(np.random.uniform(72, 93), 1),
            'Employment_Rate_pct': round(np.random.uniform(65, 96), 1),
            'Avg_Fee_PKR':         FIELD_FEES_PKR[field],
        })

field_df = pd.DataFrame(field_records)

# ── Summary Print ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print("Synthetic data generated successfully!")
print(f"\n  Yearly Enrollment Table  : {yearly_df.shape[0]} rows × {yearly_df.shape[1]} cols")
print(f"  Field-wise Enrollment    : {field_df.shape[0]} rows × {field_df.shape[1]} cols")
print(f"\n  Time Period Covered      : {YEARS[0]} – {YEARS[-1]}")
print(f"  Total Students in 2024   : {TOTAL_STUDENTS[-1]:,}")
print(f"  Computer Fields Tracked  : {len(FIELDS)}")

📈 Section 3 — Student Growth Analytics¶

Tracking total enrollment, year-over-year growth rate, and retention over 10 years.

In [4]:
# ── Student Growth Analytics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 10))
fig.suptitle('Institute Student Growth Analytics  (2015 – 2024)',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold', y=1.01)

# ── Plot 1: Total Enrollment Trend ────────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 0]
ax.plot(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Total_Students'],
        marker='o', linewidth=2.5, color='#2196F3', markersize=8)
ax.fill_between(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Total_Students'],
                alpha=0.12, color='#2196F3')
for _, row in yearly_df.iterrows():
    ax.annotate(f"{int(row['Total_Students']):,}",
                (row['Year'], row['Total_Students']),
                textcoords='offset points', xytext=(0, 10),
                ha='center', fontsize=8, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_title('Total Enrolled Students per Year', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Students')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

# ── Plot 2: Year-over-Year Growth Rate ────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 1]
colors_g = ['#4CAF50' if v >= 0 else '#F44336'
            for v in yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct']]
bars = ax.bar(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct'],
              color=colors_g, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.6)
ax.axhline(0, color='black', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')
ax.set_title('Year-over-Year Growth Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Growth Rate (%)')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
for bar, val in zip(bars, yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct']):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
            bar.get_height() + 0.3, f'{val:.1f}%',
            ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5)

# ── Plot 3: New Enrollments vs Completions ────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 0]
x_pos = np.arange(len(YEARS))
w = 0.35
ax.bar(x_pos - w/2, yearly_df['New_Enrollments'], w,
       label='New Enrollments', color='#4CAF50', edgecolor='white')
ax.bar(x_pos + w/2, yearly_df['Completions'], w,
       label='Completions', color='#FF9800', edgecolor='white')
ax.set_title('New Enrollments vs Completions per Year', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Count')
ax.set_xticks(x_pos)
ax.set_xticklabels(YEARS, rotation=45)
ax.legend()

# ── Plot 4: Retention Rate Trend ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 1]
ax.plot(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Retention_Rate_pct'],
        marker='s', linewidth=2.5, color='#9C27B0', markersize=8)
ax.fill_between(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Retention_Rate_pct'],
                alpha=0.12, color='#9C27B0')
ax.axhline(90, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, label='Target (90%)')
ax.set_title('Student Retention Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Retention Rate (%)')
ax.set_ylim(80, 100)
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('student_growth_analytics.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=120)
plt.show()

# ── Key Insights ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
total_growth = (
    (TOTAL_STUDENTS[-1] - TOTAL_STUDENTS[0]) / TOTAL_STUDENTS[0] * 100
)
avg_growth = yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct'].iloc[1:].mean()
peak_year  = yearly_df.loc[yearly_df['Growth_Rate_pct'].idxmax(), 'Year']

print("Key Insights — Student Growth:")
print(f"  Starting enrollment (2015) : {TOTAL_STUDENTS[0]:,}")
print(f"  Current enrollment  (2024) : {TOTAL_STUDENTS[-1]:,}")
print(f"  Total 10-year growth       : {total_growth:.1f}%")
print(f"  Average annual growth rate : {avg_growth:.1f}%")
print(f"  Peak growth year           : {peak_year}")
print(f"  Average retention rate     : {yearly_df['Retention_Rate_pct'].mean():.1f}%")

Identifying the most popular fields, their growth trajectories, and employment outcomes.

In [5]:
# ── Field-wise Enrollment Analytics ──────────────────────────────────────────
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 12))
fig.suptitle('Field-wise Enrollment Analytics  (2015 – 2024)',
             fontsize=15, fontweight='bold')

# ── Plot 1: All-field Trend Lines ─────────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 0]
for field in FIELDS:
    fdata = field_df[field_df['Field'] == field]
    ax.plot(fdata['Year'], fdata['Students'],
            marker='o', linewidth=2, markersize=5,
            label=field, color=FIELD_COLORS[field])
ax.set_title('Enrollment Trend by Field', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Students Enrolled')
ax.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc='upper left')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

# ── Plot 2: 2024 Distribution Donut Chart ─────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0, 1]
latest_2024 = field_df[field_df['Year'] == 2024]
ax.pie(
    latest_2024['Students'],
    labels=latest_2024['Field'],
    autopct='%1.1f%%',
    pctdistance=0.78,
    startangle=140,
    colors=[FIELD_COLORS[f] for f in latest_2024['Field']],
    wedgeprops=dict(width=0.5),
    textprops={'fontsize': 8},
)
ax.set_title('2024 Field Distribution (Donut)', fontweight='bold')

# ── Plot 3: Stacked Area — cumulative growth ──────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 0]
pivot_df = field_df.pivot(index='Year', columns='Field', values='Students')
pivot_df.plot(
    kind='area', stacked=True, ax=ax, alpha=0.72,
    color=[FIELD_COLORS[f] for f in pivot_df.columns]
)
ax.set_title('Cumulative Enrollment by Field (Stacked Area)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Total Students')
ax.legend(fontsize=7.5, loc='upper left')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

# ── Plot 4: Employment Rate by Field (2024) ───────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1, 1]
sorted_emp = latest_2024.sort_values('Employment_Rate_pct', ascending=True)
bars = ax.barh(
    sorted_emp['Field'], sorted_emp['Employment_Rate_pct'],
    color=[FIELD_COLORS[f] for f in sorted_emp['Field']],
    edgecolor='white', height=0.6
)
ax.axvline(80, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, label='80% Benchmark')
ax.set_title('Employment Rate by Field (2024)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Employment Rate (%)')
ax.set_xlim(0, 115)
for bar, val in zip(bars, sorted_emp['Employment_Rate_pct']):
    ax.text(bar.get_width() + 1, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
            f'{val:.1f}%', va='center', fontsize=9.5)
ax.legend()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('field_analytics.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=120)
plt.show()

# ── Field Insights ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
top_field    = latest_2024.loc[latest_2024['Students'].idxmax(), 'Field']
fastest      = field_df.groupby('Field').apply(
    lambda x: (x['Students'].iloc[-1] - x['Students'].iloc[0]) / x['Students'].iloc[0] * 100
).idxmax()
best_emp     = latest_2024.loc[latest_2024['Employment_Rate_pct'].idxmax(), 'Field']

print("Key Insights — Field Analysis:")
print(f"  Most popular field in 2024    : {top_field}")
print(f"  Fastest growing (2015→2024)   : {fastest}")
print(f"  Highest employment rate (2024): {best_emp} "
      f"({latest_2024['Employment_Rate_pct'].max():.1f}%)")

# ── Institute Performance Metrics ────────────────────────────────────────────
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
fig.suptitle('Institute Performance Metrics  (2015 – 2024)',
             fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

completion_rate = (yearly_df['Completions'] / yearly_df['Total_Students'] * 100).round(1)

# ── Plot 1: Completion Rate Trend ─────────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[0]
ax.plot(yearly_df['Year'], completion_rate,
        marker='D', linewidth=2.5, color='#4CAF50', markersize=8)
ax.fill_between(yearly_df['Year'], completion_rate, alpha=0.12, color='#4CAF50')
ax.axhline(completion_rate.mean(), color='orange', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2,
           label=f'Average ({completion_rate.mean():.1f}%)')
ax.set_title('Completion Rate (%)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Completion Rate (%)')
ax.set_ylim(40, 70)
ax.legend()
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

# ── Plot 2: Annual Dropout Count ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ax = axes[1]
ax.bar(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Dropouts'],
       color='#F44336', edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.6)
ax.set_title('Annual Dropout Count', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Dropout Count')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
for year, val in zip(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Dropouts']):
    ax.text(year, val + 0.5, str(int(val)), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5)

# ── Plot 3: Estimated Annual Revenue (PKR Lacs) ───────────────────────────────
revenue_df = (
    field_df.groupby('Year')
    .apply(lambda x: (x['Students'] * x['Avg_Fee_PKR']).sum())
    .reset_index(name='Revenue_PKR')
)
revenue_df['Revenue_Lacs'] = revenue_df['Revenue_PKR'] / 100_000

ax = axes[2]
ax.plot(revenue_df['Year'], revenue_df['Revenue_Lacs'],
        marker='^', linewidth=2.5, color='#FF9800', markersize=8)
ax.fill_between(revenue_df['Year'], revenue_df['Revenue_Lacs'],
                alpha=0.12, color='#FF9800')
ax.set_title('Estimated Annual Revenue (PKR Lacs)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Revenue (Lacs PKR)')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('performance_metrics.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=120)
plt.show()

print("Performance Summary:")
print(f"  Average completion rate    : {completion_rate.mean():.1f}%")
print(f"  Total dropouts (10 years)  : {yearly_df['Dropouts'].sum():,}")
print(f"  Estimated 2024 Revenue     : PKR {revenue_df.iloc[-1]['Revenue_Lacs']:.1f} Lacs")

🔮 Section 6 — Future Total Enrollment Prediction¶

Model: Polynomial Regression (degree = 2) trained on 2015–2024 data.
Forecasting total institute enrollment for 2025 – 2029.

In [7]:
# ── Build & Evaluate the Enrollment Forecast Model ───────────────────────────
X_train = yearly_df['Year'].values.reshape(-1, 1)
y_train = yearly_df['Total_Students'].values

enroll_model = Pipeline([
    ('poly', PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, include_bias=False)),
    ('lr',   LinearRegression())
])
enroll_model.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred_train = enroll_model.predict(X_train)
r2_enroll  = r2_score(y_train, y_pred_train)
mae_enroll = mean_absolute_error(y_train, y_pred_train)

print("Enrollment Prediction Model — Training Performance:")
print(f"  R² Score : {r2_enroll:.4f}  (1.00 = perfect fit)")
print(f"  MAE      : {mae_enroll:.1f} students")

# ── Forecast 2025–2029 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FUTURE_YEARS = np.array(range(2025, 2030)).reshape(-1, 1)
future_preds = enroll_model.predict(FUTURE_YEARS).astype(int)

future_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Year': range(2025, 2030),
    'Predicted_Students': future_preds
})

print("\nEnrollment Forecast (2025 – 2029):")
print(future_df.to_string(index=False))

Enrollment Prediction Model — Training Performance:

# ── Enrollment Forecast Visualization ────────────────────────────────────────
hist_years   = np.arange(2015, 2025)
bridge_years = np.arange(2024, 2030)   # overlap at 2024 for smooth join

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 6))

# Actual historical scatter + line
ax.scatter(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Total_Students'],
           color='#2196F3', s=80, zorder=5, label='Actual Enrollment')
ax.plot(yearly_df['Year'], yearly_df['Total_Students'],
        color='#2196F3', linewidth=1.8, alpha=0.55)

# Model fit curve over historical range
ax.plot(hist_years,
        enroll_model.predict(hist_years.reshape(-1, 1)),
        color='#4CAF50', linewidth=2, linestyle='--', label='Model Fit (2015–2024)')

# Forecast line
bridge_preds = enroll_model.predict(bridge_years.reshape(-1, 1)).astype(int)
ax.plot(bridge_years, bridge_preds,
        color='#FF5722', linewidth=2.5, marker='D', markersize=8,
        label='Forecast (2025–2029)')

# Confidence band (±10%)
ax.fill_between(bridge_years,
                bridge_preds * 0.90, bridge_preds * 1.10,
                alpha=0.14, color='#FF5722', label='±10% Confidence Band')

# Annotate forecast points
for yr, val in zip(range(2025, 2030), future_preds):
    ax.annotate(f'{val:,}', (yr, val),
                textcoords='offset points', xytext=(0, 12),
                ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold', color='#E64A19')

# Divider line
ax.axvline(2024.5, color='gray', linewidth=1.5, linestyle=':', alpha=0.6)
ax.text(2024.6, y_train.min() * 0.98,
        '← Historical  |  Forecast →', fontsize=8.5, color='gray', va='bottom')

ax.set_title('Total Enrollment: Historical + Forecast (2025 – 2029)',
             fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Year')
ax.set_ylabel('Total Students Enrolled')
ax.legend(loc='upper left')
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

📡 Section 7 — Field Demand Forecasting¶

Predicting which computer fields will dominate demand in 2025–2029.
A separate Polynomial Regression model is fitted for each field.

In [9]:
# ── Per-field Regression Forecasting ─────────────────────────────────────────
FORECAST_YEARS = list(range(2025, 2030))
forecast_records = []

print("Field-wise Forecast Models — R² Scores:\n")

for field in FIELDS:
    fdata = field_df[field_df['Field'] == field].sort_values('Year')
    X_f   = fdata['Year'].values.reshape(-1, 1)
    y_f   = fdata['Students'].values

    model_f = Pipeline([
        ('poly', PolynomialFeatures(degree=2, include_bias=False)),
        ('lr',   LinearRegression())
    ])
    model_f.fit(X_f, y_f)

    r2_f = r2_score(y_f, model_f.predict(X_f))
    print(f"  {field:<32}  R² = {r2_f:.4f}")

    for yr in FORECAST_YEARS:
        pred = int(max(model_f.predict([[yr]])[0], 0))
        forecast_records.append({
            'Year':               yr,
            'Field':              field,
            'Predicted_Students': pred
        })

forecast_field_df = pd.DataFrame(forecast_records)

# ── Pivot Table ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pivot_fore = forecast_field_df.pivot(
    index='Year', columns='Field', values='Predicted_Students'
)
print("\n\nField-wise Enrollment Forecast (2025 – 2029):")
print(pivot_fore.to_string())

# ── 2029 Ranking ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rank_2029 = (
    forecast_field_df[forecast_field_df['Year'] == 2029]
    .sort_values('Predicted_Students', ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
rank_2029.index += 1

print("\n\nPredicted Field Demand Ranking in 2029:")
print(rank_2029[['Field', 'Predicted_Students']].to_string())
